title: How to Pronounce Berlin Station Names - Quick Summary
items: **You do not need good German to be understood, you need a few sounds right.** Get w = v, z = ts, and ei = "eye" versus ie = "ee", and most Berlin station names stop feeling scary.

**Start with the names you will actually say out loud.** Learn your hotel's stop, your airport station, and Alexanderplatz ("ah-lex-AHN-der-plats"), where my free walking tour meets. Three names cover most of a first day.

**The umlauts ö and ü are the sounds people fear most, and they are easier than they look.** ö is the vowel in "her" with rounded lips (Schöneberg is "SHUR-nuh-bairk"), and ü is "ee" with rounded lips (Brücke is "BRUE-kuh"). Close is good enough.
**The z trap catches almost everyone.** A German z is always "ts", so Platz is "plats", Kreuzberg is "KROYTS-bairk", and Bahnhof Zoo is "tsoh", not "zoo".
**The Berlin -ow ending is the local giveaway.** Pankow is "PAN-koh" and Treptow is "TREP-toh", never rhyming with "cow". Say it the local way and you blend in fast.
**Use the Berlin Name Pronouncer below to hear any station spoken and see exactly which syllable to stress.**
